clue.text: Riddle of noted variations

definitions.meaning: a riddle is a puzzle or mystery that baffles
Elgar's orchestral work, a set of musical variations on a hidden theme, carries this title

explanation.surface: A puzzle about some set of musical variations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' means set to musical notes: Elgar's famous Variations bear the title, so the riddle and the music share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling mystery is a synonym, and Elgar's Variations on an Original Theme are known by this title.

clue.text: "——, in thy orisons Be all my sins remember'd" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: in thy orisons Be all my sins remember'd" (Hamlet)

parts.words: in thy orisons Be all my sins remember'd" (Hamlet)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Hamlet greets Ophelia with this word as she prays, at the end of his 'To be or not to be' speech

explanation.surface: A line from Hamlet with its first word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet addresses Ophelia as a maiden spirit of nature, a classical term for a lovely young woman.

clue.text: Make a bob in the service of the Church

definitions.text: Make a bob in the service of the Church

parts.words: Make a bob in the service of the Church
parts.note: to bob is to bend briefly, and in a church service worshippers bend the knee in reverence

explanation.surface: Someone earning a shilling working for the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bob' suggests the old British shilling, as if earning money in Church employment; here it is a quick bending of the knee during worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending one knee to the ground as a sign of reverence, especially in church, is this act.

clue.text: Look back in space for a circular spot

indicators.note: the reversed word is put inside the word for space

parts.note: an area is a space or expanse

indicators.note: back tells us to write the word for look in the opposite direction

parts.note: lo is an old interjection meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Searching backwards through space for a round mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look back' reads like 'look behind you', but 'back' turns the old interjection for look, and 'in' places the result inside the word for space.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring of coloured skin round a nipple, or any small ring-shaped zone, is called this in anatomy.

clue.text: Suggestions tabulated by a visionary ?

parts.note: ideas are suggestions; here the singular is used as a noun modifier, as in a tally of ideas
a list is what you get when items are tabulated or set out in order

explanation.surface: A dreamer has drawn up a table of suggestions.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: an IDEA LIST is suggestions tabulated.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary is a dreamer pursuing perfection, someone guided by lofty principles rather than practicality.

clue.text: Something to play on a record player?

definitions.text: Something to play on a record player?

parts.words: Something to play on a record player?
parts.note: not a gramophone but a musician who plays on recordings, someone who plays a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Looking for a disc to put on the gramophone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record player' suggests the gramophone; here it is a player who makes records, and what such a person plays is an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who performs on an instrument rather than singing is so called.

clue.text: The way the world is turning

definitions.text: The way the world is turning

parts.words: The way the world is turning
parts.note: literally the direction in which the Earth spins on its axis, towards the sunrise

explanation.surface: A comment on how society is changing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a remark on current trends; read literally, the Earth rotates towards the sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth spins from west to east, so its rotation heads toward the rising sun.

clue.text: Balance, one pound

definitions.meaning: the zodiac sign represented by a pair of scales
the Latin word for a pound weight, abbreviated lb

explanation.surface: Weighing out a single pound on the scales.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation lb for a pound comes from this Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign of the Scales, and the Roman unit of weight behind the abbreviation lb.

clue.text: Way out possibilities of liquid preparations

definitions.meaning: possible ways out of a problem, answers to it
mixtures of substances dissolved in liquid, as a chemist prepares

explanation.surface: Exploring far-out options among liquid mixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way out' looks like slang for outlandish, but it means an escape from a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers to problems are escapes from them, and chemists dissolve substances in liquids to make mixtures with this name.

clue.text: Nan I assume is secretary material

indicators.note: the words are raw material to be fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that Nan is good enough to be a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like 'suitable', as in executive material, but signals that NAN I ASSUME is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary assistant who takes dictation or copies manuscripts is a kind of secretary.

clue.text: Bundle of mischief

definitions.meaning: a large bound bundle, as of hay or cotton
an archaic word for evil or harm, surviving in baleful

explanation.surface: A child described as a little bundle of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic sense of harm lives on in the word 'baleful'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressed bundle of hay or cloth, and an old poetic word for evil or woe.

clue.text: He prepares the deck for action — en route for Buffalo ?

definitions.text: He prepares the deck for action — en route for Buffalo ?

parts.words: He prepares the deck for action — en route for Buffalo ?
parts.note: one who mixes a deck of cards before a game, and one who shuffles off to Buffalo, as in the old song

explanation.surface: A sailor readies a ship's deck for battle on the way to Buffalo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship; it is a pack of cards. 'Shuffle Off to Buffalo' is a 1930s American song, so a shuffling traveller is heading there.
explanation.definitionFit: One who mixes playing cards before dealing, and one who walks with a dragging gait.

clue.text: In anger I may haunt you

indicators.note: In tells us the letter I sits within the word for anger

parts.note: wrath is great anger

explanation.surface: A threat from someone furious: in my rage I may haunt you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside WRATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or spectre, the sort of apparition that might haunt a person.

clue.text: Marge's advantage

definitions.meaning: marge is a poetic word for a margin or border; the 's stands for is
having the upper hand over a rival

explanation.surface: Something that gives a woman called Marge the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marge' looks like a woman's name (or British slang for margarine); here it is the old poetic word for a margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin or border is a rim, and a slight lead over rivals is this as well.

clue.text: One to be ringed before ringing on a bicycle?

definitions.text: One to be ringed before ringing on a bicycle?

parts.words: One to be ringed before ringing on a bicycle?
parts.note: a girl's name for the one to be given a wedding ring, then the bell rung on a bicycle; together, the old song about a bicycle built for two

explanation.surface: A bride-to-be receiving her ring, then out ringing her bicycle bell.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1892 song asks Daisy for an answer to a proposal, on 'a bicycle built for two'; her name comes before the bicycle's bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The music-hall song about a bicycle made for two is known by this title.

clue.text: Running battle for gold

parts.note: a long-distance running race contested for an Olympic medal, named after an ancient Greek battle

explanation.surface: A drawn-out fight over a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running battle' looks like an idiom for a long feud; it is an Olympic road race named after the Greek battle of 490 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: The 26-mile road race, named after an ancient Greek victory, is an Olympic event with a gold medal.

clue.text: It could be responsible for a musical revolution

definitions.text: It could be responsible for a musical revolution

parts.words: It could be responsible for a musical revolution
parts.note: not a change in musical taste but the spinning platter of a gramophone that rotates a disc

explanation.surface: Something that might start a radical change in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests upheaval; read literally, it is a rotation of a record on a gramophone.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating platform of a record player spins the disc as music plays.

clue.text: Chatterbox exercises an unusually able mind

indicators.note: used unusually, the letters are put into an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A talkative person gives an exceptionally capable brain a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges ABLE MIND. The definition is what a chatterbox works hard: the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A jawbone is what a talker moves constantly, so a chatty person works it hard.

clue.text: Seize goods of boy returning to school

indicators.note: returning means the name for a boy is written backwards

parts.note: Sid is a boy's name
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Taking possessions from a lad heading back to class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun, the place the boy returns to, but it is a verb meaning to coach; 'returning' turns the boy's name round.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term: to take someone's property to force payment of a debt.

clue.text: Rebel's first word to a knight

definitions.meaning: to rebel is to ... up in revolt; the 's stands for is
the monarch dubbing a new knight says 'Arise, Sir...', the command to stand

explanation.surface: What a rebel first said to a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: At an accolade the sovereign bids the new knight to stand, so the command is the first thing said to him as a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt is to rise up, and the new knight is told to get up from kneeling.

clue.text: Tile that's not the latest style

definitions.text: Tile that's not the latest style

parts.words: Tile that's not the latest style
parts.note: tile is slang for a hat, and headgear that is not the newest is out of date

explanation.surface: A roof tile of an outdated design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old British slang for a hat. A hat that is not the latest is both literally old headgear and the phrase for something dated.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something stale and unoriginal, literally a worn-out piece of headgear.

clue.text: Cover for one of the onlookers

definitions.text: Cover for one of the onlookers

parts.words: Cover for one of the onlookers
parts.note: onlookers are taken as the organs of sight, and the cover is the fold of skin that closes over one

explanation.surface: Shelter provided for one person in a watching crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onlookers' suggests spectators; here they are the eyes, which look on.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin closing over each organ of sight acts as its lid.

clue.text: Colour is sometimes the answer

parts.note: a pale yellow colour, and a fruit that turns up on a fruit machine's reels as a losing result

explanation.surface: A remark that a colour sometimes solves a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: A pale yellow, and the citrus fruit whose name also means a dud: when things go wrong, the answer is a lemon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow shade named after a citrus fruit, also slang for a failure.

clue.text: Lost with no one on the land

definitions.text: with no one on the land
definitions.meaning: if everyone is out on the ocean, nobody remains ashore

explanation.surface: Someone lost in a place where nobody lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, the phrase says that everybody is out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for confusion, read literally as everyone away on the ocean.

clue.text: Orwellian pigs were more so than other animals

definitions.text: Orwellian pigs were more so than other animals

parts.words: Orwellian pigs were more so than other animals
parts.note: in Animal Farm the pigs declare all animals alike, but some more so than others

explanation.surface: A note on the pigs in George Orwell's satire.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal Farm's slogan reads 'All animals are ___ but some animals are more ___ than others'; the pigs are the 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Animal Farm commandment declares the animals the same in status, and the pigs claimed more of that.

clue.text: Breadth of a happy smile

definitions.meaning: the widest part of a ship is its width or breadth

explanation.surface: How wide a cheerful grin is.
explanation.walkthrough: In ship terms, the breadth of a vessel at its widest is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's width at its widest point, and a radiant grin.

clue.text: Colour of one brainy as well as athletic ?

parts.note: a brainy person is bright, clever
a blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: What colour is someone who is clever and sporty?
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a blue is awarded for representing the university at sport, so an athlete there is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid shade of azure, a hue like the sky.

clue.text: Resounding construction of a design chap

parts.note: a plan is a design or scheme
gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: An impressive building put up by a man who draws plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction of' suggests an anagram but here only links the pieces: PLAN then GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and reverberating, of a sound that rings out mournfully.

clue.text: High sounding chance of investment

definitions.meaning: a high voice or part in music, the soprano range
a bet in which winnings from one race are staked on two more

explanation.surface: A grandiose-sounding investment opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High sounding' looks like 'pretentious'; it is the top part in music. The bet is a racing accumulator over three races.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest voice part in music, and a three-race accumulator wager.
